# Figures (generated by figures/index.py; do not edit)

Run profile: **full** (5,000 Monte Carlo draws; formats png at 600 dpi). Every figure is drawn by the figures/ package from the data files listed (compute / draw separation).

## Main paper (paper_main/)

### Fig1_floor_area

**Fig1 Floor area: history and projection by demand band** — Floor area built per year by demand band: history as census-interval means (columns), the Reference projection annually from 2026 (2026 observed). Positive bands stacked up from zero, negative bands (overbuild absorbed, unconsented additions) down from zero. The black line is the floor area built (in scope), annual 1992-2050 (history from consents, projection from 2026); the grey caps on the history columns are the census-interval means. 2026 overbuild: observed 2026 building above need, fading from 2027 and absorbed by 2035.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig1_floor_area.png`
- Data: `data/baseline/bands_history.csv`, `data/baseline/bands_annual.csv`, `data/baseline/annual.csv`, `data/baseline/overbuild_2026.json`
- This run: Completions = 0.945 x consents lagged 17 months (median consent-to-completion time 1.27-1.53 yr, Jones, Greenaway-McGrevy & Crow 2025; consistent with the Stats NZ Experimental building indicators). Households after the 2023 census = ERP / household-size path (Stats NZ DHE not used). Pipeline years 2026, 2027: building observed (consents to July 2026); the part above modelled need fades from 2028 (ρ = 0.43) and is absorbed by 2035. 2026 population: Stats NZ ERP nowcast. Six display bands (data/bands_display_map.csv); market balance = unexplained building + retirement villages (out of scope) + overbuild / pipeline excess + overbuild absorbed + surplus kept vacant. Negative bands drawn down from zero: Smaller households, Market balance, Vacancy, Net replacement. Black line: floor area built (in scope), annual 1992-2050 (straight segments between year centres; history 1992-2025 from consents, projection from 2026); grey caps: census-interval means of the history columns (the mean of the annual values over each interval, checked). 2026-2050: 81.5 Mm².

### Fig2_reference_carbon

**Fig2 Embodied carbon of the Reference** — Annual embodied carbon of the Reference 2026-2050 by (a) demand band, (b) material and (c) life-cycle stage; (d) cumulative 2026-2050 as three attached columns of the same total by demand band, material and stage (negative demand bands outlined, hanging down to the total). Materials and stages are never negative.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig2_reference_carbon.png`
- Data: `data/baseline/bands_annual.csv`, `data/baseline/annual_by_material.csv`, `data/baseline/annual_by_stage.csv`
- This run: 2026-2050: 19,761 kt CO₂e; (d) the demand column: positive bands stacked to 19,761 kt, negative bands outlined, hanging down to the total.

### Fig3_reference_boundaries

**Fig3 The Reference against the planetary boundaries** — (a) Annual carbon, Monte Carlo median with 50% and 90% bands, against the acquired-rights (AR) and ability-to-pay (AtP) boundaries and their zones; (b) cumulative carbon 2026-2050 with its Monte Carlo 90% interval (5th-95th percentile of the cumulative carbon) and 50% interval (25th-75th), the AR and AtP budgets, and the committed emissions after 2050: C1-C4 and B2/B4 after 2050, the latter a range (lower = 2050 factors held, upper = 2025 factors).

- Files: `paper_main/Fig3_reference_boundaries.png`
- Data: `data/aesa/annual.csv`, `data/montecarlo/annual_REF.csv`, `data/montecarlo/draws_REF.csv`, `data/baseline/projection.json`
- This run: Cumulative 2026-2050 19,761 kt (LoE AR 4.46, AtP 17.8); Monte Carlo 90% interval 14,575-25,503 kt (5th-95th percentile of the cumulative carbon of the draws), 50% interval 17,558-21,986 kt; committed after 2050 (drawn at the lower bound): C1-C4 4,410 kt (2025 factors) and B2/B4 after 2050 3,091 kt (2050 factors held; 3,810 kt with 2025 factors). Moderate / Ambitious Pathway and TL: deterministic runs. Lines are shape-preserving (PCHIP) interpolation through the annual values, not smoothed across the observed -> modelled join after 2027; bands: Monte Carlo 90% band pchip, Monte Carlo 50% band pchip.

### Fig4_pathways

**Fig4 The Pathways: the sequential waterfalls** — Sequential waterfalls of cumulative carbon 2026-2050 from the Reference, levers added in PAS 2080 order: (a) L1 ... L9 at Moderate -> Moderate Pathway; (b) at Ambitious -> Ambitious Pathway; (c) TL1 ... TL9 cumulative -> Theoretical Limit. Each step is one bar coloured by strategy with its net change; AR (solid) and AtP (dotted) budgets with their zones; order-free Shapley values in Fig6.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig4_pathways.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/annual.csv`, `data/pathways/waterfall.csv`, `data/pathways/waterfall_tl_from_reference.csv`
- This run: Cumulative LoE AR: REF 4.46, pathway-moderate 3.23, pathway-ambitious 2.32, TL 1.00. (a-c) Reference 19,761 kt -> Moderate Pathway 14,302 kt, Ambitious Pathway 10,267 kt, Theoretical Limit 4,423 kt; budgets AR 4,427 kt, AtP 1,113 kt. Steps in PAS 2080 order; each step is credited with what remains after the higher-priority measures; order-free Shapley values in Fig6. Net-positive steps: none.

### Fig5_solution_space

**Fig5 The solution space** — Cumulative level of exceedance of AR over uniform cuts of 2027-2050 floor area (x) and of carbon per m2 (y) (after Horup et al. 2025), axes -5% to 100%, with S1-S3 (Moderate filled, Ambitious hollow), the Moderate / Ambitious Pathway and the Theoretical Limit; analytic LoE AR contours and the exact AR line. Right: the LoE AR ruler (log) with the Reference, the Pathways, TL, AR = 1, the plane floor (the 2026 observed cohort alone) and AtP.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig5_solution_space.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/solution_space.csv`, `data/pathways/backcast.json`, `data/pathways/runs.csv`
- This run: LoE AR = [1,207 + 18,554 (1 - x)(1 - y)] / 4,427 kt; C_2026 = the 2026 cohort's emissions in the window; plane floor C_2026 / B_AR = 0.273 (the lowest LoE AR at x or y = 100%); AtP = B_AtP / B_AR = 0.251 lies below the floor, so the AtP contour is outside the plotted square (y = 100.5% at x = 0). Axes -5% to 85%.

### Fig6_shapley_levers

**Fig6 What each lever removes** — Shapley values within each combined game (Reference -> Moderate Pathway, -> Ambitious Pathway, -> TL; exact, 512 subsets) on cumulative carbon 2026-2050: rows grouped by PAS 2080 strategy (S1 Avoid, S2 Switch, S3 Improve) in the lever order and coloured by strategy; filled bar Moderate, hollow bar Ambitious, large deep-green dot TL. The TL dots are Shapley values within the TL game (all nine levers at their limit), so they include each lever's interactions at the limit; L5 (occupancy density) interacts with L4 (extra space): both act on the floor area per dwelling.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig6_shapley_levers.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/shapley.csv`
- This run: (a) Standalone: each lever alone vs the Reference (not additive). (b) Shapley shares within each combined game (Reference -> Moderate Pathway, -> Ambitious Pathway, -> TL; 512 subsets per game); the TL shares include interactions at the limit (L5 with L4). Game totals (= Reference - Pathway / TL): moderate 5,460 kt, ambitious 9,494 kt, tl 15,339 kt.

### Fig7_uncertainty

**Fig7 Uncertainty** — (a) One-at-a-time ranges of the Reference cumulative LoE AR 2026-2050, each input at its low and high end per its definition (population rows move the budgets with the path; AR base-window rows move the AR budget only); not additive, not a joint interval. (b) The Reference, the Moderate and Ambitious Pathways and the Theoretical Limit: cumulative LoE AR against the 2050 New Zealand population on the same paired Monte Carlo draws, P(LoE AR <= 1) of each with its Wilson 95% interval, LoE = 1, and the population at which the Theoretical Limit has P(LoE AR <= 1) = 50% (Firth logistic; bootstrap 95% CI).

- Files: `paper_main/Fig7_uncertainty.png`

- This run: (b) The flat left tail: the lowest-population draws, where re-used dwellings meet all need (zero-build years); its carbon floor is the 2026-27 pipeline plus maintenance. (a) Reference LoE AR 4.464; population rows move the budgets with the path; the AR base-window row moves the AR budget only; one-at-a-time ranges are not additive. (b) P(TL within AR) = 0.499 (Wilson 0.485-0.513; n = 5,000); P(LoE AR <= 1) on the same paired draws: REF 0.0000 (Wilson 0.0000-0.0008), pathway_moderate 0.0000 (Wilson 0.0000-0.0008), pathway_ambitious 0.0002 (Wilson 0.0000-0.0011), TL 0.4988 (Wilson 0.4849-0.5127); threshold 6.614 M (95% CI 6.611-6.616 M; Firth penalised likelihood (MLE does not exist), 2000 resamples).

### ED4_one_at_a_time

**ED4 One at a time: cumulative embodied carbon 2026-2050 of the Reference** — One-at-a-time ranges of the Reference cumulative embodied carbon 2026-2050, grouped by category; each input at its low (blue) and high (orange) end, a single alternative case grey, intermediate cases as ticks; not additive, not a joint interval. Not shown (kept in the data file): household size held flat after 2043 (the Reference is also held constant after 2043, with a zero slope imposed at 2043), the overbuild gap against the 2026 requirement, no census under-construction correction, the maintenance event timing L / n, and the version-history rows (their changes are in the note). What each row changes compared with the Reference: Household size (2018–23 pace): household size continues linearly from 2023 at the 2018–2023 census-interval pace instead of the Stats NZ household-size path rebased on 2023. Population (5th–95th pct.): Stats NZ 2024-base stochastic projection, 5th / 95th percentile path instead of the median. Household size (smaller–larger households): Stats NZ Low / High household-size variant (smaller / larger households) instead of the Medium variant. Household size after 2043: end-slope taper: from the shape-preserving (PCHIP) end slope at 2043 the slope tapers to zero over 5 years, instead of a zero slope imposed at 2043 and household size held constant after 2043. Household size after 2043: secant-slope taper: the last published interval (2038–2043) linear at its secant slope, the slope then tapering to zero over 5 years, instead of a zero slope imposed at 2043 and household size held constant after 2043. 2026 overbuild booked as stock-neutral redevelopment: the 2026 overbuild (building above need in 2026–2027 and its continuation, fading at ρ = 0.43) replaces existing dwellings instead of adding to the stock: no surplus, so no absorption payback and no soil carbon loss on it. Dwelling-size reference window 2016–2025: new-dwelling size held at its 2016–2025 mean per typology instead of the 2023–2025 mean. Completion rate (0.93–0.96): 0.93 / 0.96 of consented dwellings completed instead of 0.945. Vacancy rate: 1986–2023 census mean: the mean of the 1986–2023 censuses on one definition instead of the 2023 census value (5.39%). Overbuild absorbed (by 2030–by 2045): the 2026 overbuild absorbed by 2030 / 2045 instead of 2035. Completion lag (15–19 months): consents lagged 15 / 19 months instead of 17. No 2026 data (consents to Dec 2025): consents to December 2025 and the projected 2026 population instead of consents to July 2026 and the observed 2026 population growth. Replacement (Low–Very High): Low: the 1991–2023 long-run net rate throughout; High (tick): the 2018–2023 rate persists; Very High: the 1991–2023 census-interval trend continues; instead of the 2018–2023 rate fading to the long-run rate with a 10-year half-life. Replacement half-life (5–15 yr): 5 / 15 years instead of 10. Soil order (Raw–Organic): the soil carbon loss of the lowest (Raw) / highest (Organic) soil order on every new footprint instead of the area-weighted mean over the soil orders of the Auckland land zoned for urbanisation. Single case study (lowest–highest): the materials factor of the lowest / highest single case study of each typology instead of the pooled typology factor. Frozen technology (2025 factors held): every factor held at 2025 instead of A1–A3 on the item paths of Horup et al. (2025) and A4–A5 falling 1% per year. Carbon factors (jackknife): the lowest / highest pooled materials factor when each case study is left out in turn, instead of the pooled factor (a spread, not a confidence interval). NZ-made electricity-intensive items held at 2025 factors: items made in New Zealand with electricity-intensive production held at 2025 instead of following their Horup et al. (2025) path. A4–A5 decarbonisation (own path–held at 2025): A4–A5 on each item's own Horup et al. (2025) path / held at 2025 instead of the generic 1% per year decline (Resch et al. 2021). Soil carbon loss on all floor area, incl. replacement: soil carbon loss also on replacement floor area instead of none on rebuilt footprints. Proxy-mapped items held at 2025 factors: items mapped to a proxy material held at 2025 instead of following the proxy's path.

- Files: `paper_extended/ED4_one_at_a_time.png`
- Data: `data/sensitivity/reference_carbon.csv`
- This run: Reference 19,761 kt. One at a time: not additive, not a joint interval. "No effect": every case within 0.01% of the Reference. Not shown: the version-history rows (completion rate 0.95 and lag 0 months of MODEL v3.3; the never-absorbed overbuild of MODEL v2.1) and household size held flat after 2043 (the Reference is also held constant after 2043 and differs only by the zero slope imposed at 2043) (+0.0047%); the overbuild gap measured against the 2026 requirement (+0.0034%); no census under-construction correction (+0.0000%); maintenance event timing L / n (-0.7560%) (in the data file). ### ED5_boundary_sensitivity

**ED5 Boundary definitions and allocation: cumulative LoE of AR and of AtP** — One-at-a-time ranges of the Reference cumulative level of exceedance 2026-2050 of (a) acquired rights (AR) and (b) ability to pay (AtP): boundary definitions, allocation, population and replacement. Not shown (kept in the data file): α = 1 (Hjalsted et al. SI tables) and the raw Stats NZ 2024-base median population. What each row changes compared with the Reference: Carrying capacity: 1 W/m² boundary (not 2 °C): 1 W/m² planetary boundary (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015), safe operating space 3.61 × 10¹² kg CO₂e per year, instead of the 2 °C carrying capacity (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015), 6.81 × 10¹² (the same global impact); both budgets move. AR base window (5–34 yr): mean sector emissions over 5 / 20 / 34 years (2021–2025, 2006–2025, 1992–2025) instead of 10 years (2016–2025); AR only. Economic allocation measure: GDP per capita, current US$: GDP per capita in current US$ instead of GDP per capita at purchasing-power parity, constant 2021 international $ (World Bank WDI); AtP only. Sector share: ratio of sums (not mean of ratios): FCE share of GDP in the sector share: the ratio of the summed FCE to the summed GDP of the 40 quarters 2016–2025 instead of the mean of the 40 quarterly FCE/GDP ratios 2016–2025; AtP only. Population (5th–95th pct.): Stats NZ 2024-base 5th / 95th percentile path instead of the median; carbon and both budgets move together. Population source: UN WPP 2024 median: UN WPP 2024 median for New Zealand instead of the model's population path (the Stats NZ 2024-base median from the observed 2025 level, with the observed 2026 growth); budgets only. Replacement (Low–Very High): as in Extended Data Fig. 4 (carbon only; the budgets are unchanged). Replacement half-life (5–15 yr): as in Extended Data Fig. 4 (carbon only).

- Files: `paper_extended/ED5_boundary_sensitivity.png`
- Data: `data/sensitivity/planetary_boundary.csv`, `data/aesa/results.json`
- This run: Reference cumulative LoE of AR 4.46, of AtP 17.76; AR base window central 2016-2025. 'No effect': within 0.01% of the Reference (the economic-allocation rows move AtP only, the AR base window moves AR only). Not shown: α = 1 (Hjalsted et al. SI tables); the raw Stats NZ 2024-base median population (in the data file). Row notes: Carrying capacity: 1 W/m² boundary (not 2 °C): 1 W/m² planetary boundary (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015), safe operating space 3.61 × 10¹² kg CO₂e per year, instead of the 2 °C carrying capacity (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015), 6.81 × 10¹² (the same global impact); both budgets move. AR base window (5–34 yr): mean sector emissions over 5 / 20 / 34 years (2021–2025, 2006–2025, 1992–2025) instead of 10 years (2016–2025); AR only. Economic allocation measure: GDP per capita, current US$: GDP per capita in current US$ instead of GDP per capita at purchasing-power parity, constant 2021 international $ (World Bank WDI); AtP only. Sector share: ratio of sums (not mean of ratios): FCE share of GDP in the sector share: the ratio of the summed FCE to the summed GDP of the 40 quarters 2016–2025 instead of the mean of the 40 quarterly FCE/GDP ratios 2016–2025; AtP only. Population (5th–95th pct.): Stats NZ 2024-base 5th / 95th percentile path instead of the median; carbon and both budgets move together. Population source: UN WPP 2024 median: UN WPP 2024 median for New Zealand instead of the model's population path (the Stats NZ 2024-base median from the observed 2025 level, with the observed 2026 growth); budgets only. Replacement (Low–Very High): as in Extended Data Fig. 4 (carbon only; the budgets are unchanged). Replacement half-life (5–15 yr): as in Extended Data Fig. 4 (carbon only).

### SF2_stock_vacancy

**SF2 Vacancy, dwellings per year by component and the vacancy definition**

- Files: `supplementary/calibration/SF2_stock_vacancy.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D05_stock_and_vacancy.json`, `data/figure_source/D06_vacancy_definition.json`
- This run: a: The vacancy-rate parameter is held at its published 2023 census value (5.39%; on the consistent definition 2023 is the series maximum, 5.38%, minimum 4.01% in 1996); the 2026 overbuild raises implied stock vacancy temporarily and is absorbed by 2035, so implied vacancy returns to the parameter (5.39% in 2050). c: the unconsented additions each vacancy definition requires to close the stock identity (BRANZ demolition rate); counting residents-away dwellings as vacant requires implausibly many. b: History: one bar per census interval (interval means; vacancy on one definition, the pooled 2018/2023 empty share, 49.2% of unoccupied dwellings); between censuses annual detail is not identified. Faint bar: 2024–2025, households consent-derived. Projection annual, lighter. History: net replacement is census-measured, the rate of the census dwelling-count identity of each interval (SF3; under-construction corrected) x the previous year's stock, the quantity the model uses (2024–2025: the latest rate carried). Projection: demolition replacement, unconsented additions (negative), the recent replacement surge, retirement villages (negative), the 2026 overbuild and the overbuild absorbed (negative payback). Negative parts are outlined, hanging from the top of the positive stack; each bar ends at its net total (tick). Unexplained building (faded red; its value per interval in the row at the top, thousand dwellings per year): building not explained by household formation, vacancy and census-measured replacement: redevelopment not captured by the census counts, error in the household estimates, or residual; it may be negative.

- Data: `data/figure_source/D14_hindcast.json`, `data/baseline/validation.json`
- This run: Rolling-origin hindcast of dwellings built (cumulative), each origin projected with the information available then; errors at the end of each window, vacancy on the consistent definition. The four replacement variants use only the census intervals ending at or before the origin: Low the long-run dwelling-count rate, Reference the last intercensal rate fading to it (10-year half-life), High the last rate held, Very High the weighted linear trend of the interval rates (3, 4 and 5 intervals at the 2006, 2013 and 2018 origins). d: building of the first year the run without 2026 data models, observed in the pipeline (consents lagged), against that run.

### SF7_completion_lag

**SF7 Annual floor area by demand group: zero- and 17-month completion lag**

- Files: `supplementary/validation/SF7_completion_lag.png`
- Data: `data/diagnostics/lag_comparison_annual.csv`
- This run: Both runs use identical source files and demographic paths; only the monthly consent-to-completion lag changes. Zero lag treats a rolling 12-month consent estimate as the 2026 build proxy; it is not a count of completed calendar-2026 homes. The 17-month run uses complete observed consent cohorts for 2026 and 2027. Lag-specific historical completion timing and replacement calibration are recomputed consistently, so panel c is not like-for-like in replacement: the net replacement rate is re-estimated from the census dwelling counts with each run's completion timing (2018-2023 interval: 0.301%/yr at zero lag, with the census under-construction correction, against 0.173%/yr at 17 months), and the difference in c is that recalibration, not the timing of building itself (MODEL v4.3.1, investigation B3).
